aggressive_definition: Advanced versus localized prostate cancer and high-grade (Gleason score ≥7) versus low-grade (Gleason score <7) prostate cancer at diagnosis.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: In case-only analyses, we used unconditional logistic regression to quantify associations of total 25(OH)D with stage (advanced vs. localized) and Gleason grade (high-grade (≥7) vs. low-grade (<7)).
study_design: Case-control study nested within the ProtecT prostate-cancer testing trial, with additional case-only analyses of stage and grade
cohort_total_n_excerpt: We included 1,447 prostate cancer cases (153 advanced, 469 high-grade) and 1,449 healthy controls.
reason: The abstract evaluates overall PSA-detected prostate cancer using healthy controls and separately evaluates aggressive characteristics present at diagnosis. The aggressive analyses compare advanced with localized cases and high-grade with low-grade cases; they are not postdiagnosis progression or survival analyses. The aggressive case count records the 153 advanced cases, while 469 high-grade cases were also reported.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: There was no evidence of a linear association between total 25(OH)D and prostate cancer (p=0.44) or of an increased risk of prostate cancer with high and low vitamin D levels.
estimate_classifications.reason: The supplied row concerns overall prostate cancer cases versus healthy controls. It must not be relabeled aggressive merely because separate stage- and grade-specific analyses were performed.

additional_estimates.comparison: Deficient (<12 ng/mL) versus adequate (20-<30 ng/mL) circulating total 25(OH)D
additional_estimates.effect_excerpt: There was evidence that men deficient in vitamin D had a 2-fold increased risk of advanced versus localized cancer (OR for deficient vs. adequate total 25(OH)D=2.33, 95% CI: 1.26, 4.28)
additional_estimates.count_excerpt: We included 1,447 prostate cancer cases (153 advanced, 469 high-grade) and 1,449 healthy controls.
additional_estimates.endpoint_definition: Advanced versus localized prostate cancer in the case-only analysis
